known_final_diagnosis: The diagnosis of GPA was based on the presence of suggestive clinical signs, notably the notion of hemoptysis, anemia, and suggestive appearance in the scan: multifocal ground glass with respect for the periphery, association of septal lines (crazy paving), and the presence of siderophages in the BAL. The diagnosis was also based on the American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) 2022 classification criteria: the presence of c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities (5 points) (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female presented with diffuse interstitial lung disease, chronic anemia, altered general condition, stage II dyspnea, and low-grade hemoptysis. Initial chest X-ray showed interstitial syndrome with bilateral infiltrative opacities. Thoracic CT revealed diffuse bilateral ground glass with septal and non-septal thickening (crazy paving), more marked in the upper lobes with subpleural sparing, suggestive of alveolar hemorrhage. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) showed histiocytic macrophagic alveolitis with hemosiderosis. Immunological workup confirmed the presence of c-ANCA. The diagnosis of GPA was established based on these findings, fulfilling the American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) 2022 classification criteria, specifically the presence of c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities (5 points).
